title: How a Remote Company Builds AI Fluency — Em Shreve, Automattic
talk_summary: Automattic runs two-week in-person AI enablement cohorts (50% facilitated learning, 50% real project work) to upskill engineers and non-engineers, with a multiplier/champions model and shared MCP/skill infrastructure.

takeaways.technique: Shared internal MCP server as a platform
takeaways.what_they_do: They run one internal MCP server ('context automattic') where teams rapidly add tool sets and layer governance/observability, and cohort projects extend it rather than each building standalone integrations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have our own uh internal uh MCP server called context automatic. And this allows us um to rapidly add new tooling sets for MCPs

takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain a skills directory usable across Codex, Claude, opencode etc. rather than prescribing one tool, so skills are portable across model/harness choices.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we wanted to build our skills directory in a way that can be used across all of those

takeaways.what_they_do: They designate top practitioners as guides who run local workshops and 'AI ride-alongs' showing their actual workflow, plus an always-on help channel staffed by program alumni.
takeaways.evidence_quote: seeing someone in your similar role or um in in a similar job to you, being able to see how they use it
takeaways.numbers: 7 cohorts of ~45 people; ~600 people target (~2/3 of engineers); ~10 local events

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure adoption with repeated surveys at 72 hours, 30 days, and 90 days, tracking intentionality, flow, sharing, and per-topic lift.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we'll do one 72 hours after uh 30 days after and 90 days after
